When Sacred Idol spawns (the Idol with a tether to the boss), kill it ASAP!

payload.name: Angra Mainyu
payload.summary: Alterna colores en Double Vision, mira fuera durante Mortal Gaze y sal del sector seleccionado por Roulette.
payload.summary_es: Alterna colores en Double Vision, mira fuera durante Mortal Gaze y sal del sector seleccionado por Roulette.
encounter_notes: Double Vision, a floor-covering AoE that is split into red and white, which gives a stacking debuff depending on what colour you're standing on. The white AoE will give a "Sullen" debuff and the red AoE will give an "Ireful" debuff. The stacks will reset to 1 if you alternate which colour you stand on when it hits. If you get 2 stacks of the debuff you will take 2.5k damage. If you get 3 stacks you will die.

When he casts Mortal Gaze, anyone looking in his direction will receive a Doom debuff that kills you in 10 seconds. Stand on whichever one of the four circular platforms that is lit up to remove this debuff. You can also turn away from the boss when he casts the ability to completely avoid the Doom debuff.

Roulette, signified by a finger and a cone that rotates clockwise around the boss room, occurs when 4 Final Hourglasses spawn at the outer edge of the room. Kill the 4 Final Hourglass one by one. To avoid being killed, do not stand in the quarter that is lit up when the last Final Hourglass dies. As long as all four of the Hourglasses die, you will be able to run out of that section if you happen to be in it.

Level 100 Flare: Red ball spawns on a player and a red circle appears on the ground. This ability tethers several players to 1 player. You need to run out of the circle to cancel the ability. Players in the red circle will all take massive damage if the total number of players in the circle is an even number.

Level 150 Death: Purple ball spawns on a player and a purple circle appears on the ground. This ability tethers several players to 1 player. You need to run out of the circle to cancel the ability. Players in the purple circle will all die if the total number of players in the circle is a multiple of 3.
Adds should be killed or they will deal powerful raidwide damage.
===The Nape===
Enemies: Queen Scylla

Scylla will use Ancient Flare, an attack that will do raid-wide damage if not interrupted. Six Forbidden Gates will spawn, three west and three east, which will slowly begin casting Void Call. If not defeated before they finish the cast, they will turn into a Thor, which has no notable mechanics.

After defeating them, a fake Treasure Coffer will appear, which will turn into a Xande's Clone when opened, who will use Ancient Quaga, another interruptible attack. Six more Forbidden Gates will spawn, although two of them will be larger. The larger gates will turn into a Jormungand if not defeated in time, which has no notable mechanics.

payload.name: Five-headed Dragon
payload.summary: Evita hielo expansivo, controla slimes y orbes, mata las cinco cabezas durante Discordance y deja de actuar durante Heatwave.
payload.summary_es: Evita hielo expansivo, controla slimes y orbes, mata las cinco cabezas durante Discordance y deja de actuar durante Heatwave.
encounter_notes: Ice Floor's AoE expands if it hits a player. When you see a white, circular swirl on the ground, run away. Anyone who steps in these will be inflicted with Deep Freeze for several seconds and unable to move or take actions.

An orange circle AoE telegraph will leave behind a poison puddle that will spawn multiple Poison Slimes. These need to be killed to stop them from joining together and casting silence (The Last Song) on the entire raid. Killing them causes them to burst into poison resistance buffs. At least one player should stand in the puddle to prevent more slimes from spawning and turning into a Toxic Slime. This must be killed or it will explode for high damage (Fermata) and inflicting a stack of Vulnerability Up.

When the boss channels Discordance you have to kill the 5 extra heads that appear or the raid will wipe. Defeat them all with AoE attacks. The boss could use this multiple times, so stay on your toes if your DPS is slower.

The boss will occasionally mark a player with a stack marker. When this happens, a small number of players (usually 3-5) need to stack on this player to split the damage. If this does not happen, the player will receive 9999 damage.

When you see Prominence orbs appear, red circles spawn on the ground followed by red or white balls, kill the orbs ASAP before they explode (Radiance) and deal damage, inflicting stacks of Vulnerability Up.

An untargetable Dragonfire Fly will tether a player and inflicts a stacking Suppuration debuff, reducing their maximum HP and increasing damage taken. The player needs to run and touch another player to transfer the tether before the debuff kills them.
Heatwave is a raid-wide attack used when the boss' HP is low. For 5 seconds, every action you make will deal 500 damage, so players should stop moving and attacking.
===The Jaws===
Enemies: Howling Atomos (left), Moaning Atomos (center), and Roaring Atomos (right).

Each party should split off, with A going left, B middle, and C right, to isolated platforms, each containing an Atomos. The three different Atomos will periodically synchronize their HP, so they will all die together regardless of differences in DPS.

A random player will be marked with a crosshair, indicating the Atomos will use an untelegraphed conal AoE on them that will suck in anyone hit. Ideally, the marked player will jump to the ring below, and other players will avoid the marked player. Anyone sucked in will then be spit off the platform to the lower ring, granting a vulnerability down Vulnerability Down buff to the Atomos. A player on the upper platform will need to stand on the glowing white circle to activate a jump pad allowing lower players to return to the top. If all players in the entire alliance get stuck on the lower rings, the raid will wipe.

The Atomos will also use Shockwave, an untelegraphed radial knockback. Stand right under the mob when it's casting Shockwave because if you're not in that purple puddle you will get knocked off. The knockback can be prevented with Arm's Length or Surecast.
A Sacrificed Soldier add will also spawn on each platform and should be defeated. A spinning yellow disc will also move across the platform and should be avoided to prevent damage.

payload.name: Cerberus
payload.summary: Cuando se suelte, hazte Mini antes de entrar al charco y ser devorado; destruye las paredes del estómago y vuelve a colocar las dos cadenas.
payload.summary_es: Cuando se suelte, hazte Mini antes de entrar al charco y ser devorado; destruye las paredes del estómago y vuelve a colocar las dos cadenas.
encounter_notes: When Cerberus becomes unchained and starts Thrashing, a group of players (usually Alliance B, plus any DPS that want to) needs to execute the following in order:
Stand next to the Gastric Juice mob to get hit by File:Minimum icon1.png Mini spell and shrunk to a small size.
Stand in the purple puddle to get Devoured by the boss. (Do not stand in the puddle if you don't have the File:Minimum icon1.png Mini debuff, as Cerberus will instantly kill you.)
Once inside, kill the adds on the wall in his stomach.

When the adds are dead he will stop thrashing, and will slump to the ground in pain. Groups outside the stomach need to use the two tethers to re-chain him while he is weakened - both tethers need to be re-attached to each of the Open Fetters on his sides by interacting with them. Players who pick up the chains should not linger too long with these.

If there are fewer than 5 living players outside the belly, Cerberus will immediately eject all players inside him without collapsing. FFXIV Mythbusters | What if Cerberus Ate EVERYONE? - Caetsu Chaiji Ch.

If his belly adds are not killed or he is not re-chained, Cerberus' haste Haste and Damage Up Damage Up buffs will stack out of control and wipe the raid. There are two meta strategies for handling this mechanic:
====DPS Rush====
* All DPS should get swallowed to burn down the stomach walls as quickly as possible. One (1) healer joins them so they don't die.

DPS Rush is both faster and safer, as B alliance can be people who don't know how to get in the belly or are new. The ABC strat below is just included for reference and should only be used if most of the alliance insists on doing it.
====ABC = Adds/Belly/Chains====
* Alliance A should pull and kill the adds, Wolfsbane, which are quite dangerous if not tanked because their attack is a large cleave poison.
* Alliance B should go into Cerberus' stomach.
* Alliance C should tank Cerberus, and focus on re-chaining Cerberus whilst he is weakened.
Due to gear creep, DPS Rush is more common nowadays.
Cerberus has a Tail Swipe attack that hits players behind him in a cone.
Ululation is a roar that causes players who are not around other players to become feared for 15 seconds. Stay near your party members to avoid the fear effect.

payload.name: Cloud of Darkness
payload.summary: Corre por el borde con Feint Particle Beam, sal del centro cuando desaparezca, ocupa torres y mata nubes antes de que sean absorbidas.
payload.summary_es: Corre por el borde con Feint Particle Beam, sal del centro cuando desaparezca, ocupa torres y mata nubes antes de que sean absorbidas.
encounter_notes: Cloud of Darkness targets the tank with a powerful auto-attack that also deals damage over time, so keep your tank safe.

A random player will get targeted with red crosshairs (Feint Particle Beam). After a few seconds, blasts will start chasing after the target player at running speed damaging anyone nearby. Each blast adds a Vulnerability Up debuff and it kills you quickly if you stop moving. The player targeted should run towards the outside edge of the area, away from all other players.

Any time she moves around the ring, she fires a massive laser (Zero-form Particle Beam) through the center of the area. When she disappears, immediately move to the sides. This attack will give a Vulnerability Up debuff. This does not have a ground telegraph.

Throughout the fight, she will spawn comets on yellow circle markers (towers). At least one person should stand in each one before the comet reaches the ground or the raid suffers moderate damage (several empty comets will wipe the raid). The person in the comet area will take a small hit.

Mid-fight, the floor of the area will light up and smaller Dark Cloud and larger Dark Storm adds will start spawning. Kill them before they get close enough for the boss to eat them and gain stacks of Damage Up, or she will wipe you if she eats enough. The smaller adds will give her one stack, while the larger attacks will give three. The clouds can be affected by Heavy but not by Bind. If anyone stands between the clouds and CoD, it will add the Heavy effect to them. After the cloud phase is done she will do a raid-wide attack.

Next, she will spawn 3 Hypercharged Clouds in a triangle formation. These clouds have a box shaped outline around them and cannot be damaged outside the box after a few seconds, so move into one of the boxes and kill the clouds. A, B, and C should have their own cloud and this can be marked ahead of time with waymarks, although it is not critical to evenly split the alliances. If they are not killed before Particle Beam finishes casting, they will explode for massive damage.

If your raid DPS is very low, worm adds (Shadowlurkers) will spawn around the area before the cloud phase. Hitting them once or twice causes them to disappear. The worms add many debuffs like Morbol's Bad Breath to anyone standing too close to them. Stay away and let the ranged DPS handle. If they are left alive for too long, they will target random players with a massive AoE (Black Thunder) that deals damage and inflicts a stack of Vulnerability Up.

payload.name: Antivirus X
payload.summary: The boss has an omnidirectional hitbox and does not move. *Immune Response: A telegraphed wide frontal conal AoE in front of the boss (leaving the sides or behind safe). Will also spawn a dangerous AoE around the arena. *Immune Response: A telegraphed wide AoE that now hits to the sides and behind (leaving the front safe).
encounter_notes: The boss has an omnidirectional hitbox and does not move.
*Immune Response: A telegraphed wide frontal conal AoE in front of the boss (leaving the sides or behind safe). Will also spawn a dangerous AoE around the arena.
*Immune Response: A telegraphed wide AoE that now hits to the sides and behind (leaving the front safe).
* Spawns five untargetable purple nodes (Interferon R and Interferon C) around the boss on the cardinals and intercardinals.

**A purple line will begin connecting the five nodes starting from the northwest or northeast, indicating the order in which they will resolve an AoE. Each node will also be given a green indicator: A plus indicates a plus-shaped AoE (Pathocross Purge) originating from the node, and a circle indicates a donut AoE (Pathocircuit Purge) originating from the node.
**Players must pay attention to the green indicator and dodge the AoEs in the order they resolve, as they have late ground telegraphs.
**During the last set of AoEs, the boss will begin casting another Immune Response (front or side/rear cleave).
*Quarantine: Telegraphed AoE tankbuster (Disinfection) and a stack marker on a random player. The tank should stay out while the other players stack together.
* Similar to before, but the boss will now use Immune Response twice as the node AoEs resolve. Players must consider the order of the mechanics and dodge accordingly.
**The order is: Node 1 > Node 2 + Immune Response > Node 3 > Node 4 > Node 5 > Immune Response
**Using Sprint is recommended.
*Cytolysis: Party-wide damage

payload.name: Amalgam
payload.summary: *Electrowave: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edges of the arena. *Disassembly: Amalgam divides into parts. Party-wide magical damage and the boss will divide into parts and become a smaller node. A line of electricity will begin outlining a triangle in half of the arena, indicating a late telegraph AoE. *Amalgam becomes whole again.
encounter_notes: *Electrowave: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edges of the arena.

*Disassembly: Amalgam divides into parts. Party-wide magical damage and the boss will divide into parts and become a smaller node. A line of electricity will begin outlining a triangle in half of the arena, indicating a late telegraph AoE.
*Amalgam becomes whole again.
*Centralized Current: An electric line will spawn through where the boss is facing, indicating a late telegraphed line AoE in that direction, leaving the sides of the boss's hitbox safe.
*Split Current: Similar to Centralized Current, but will now indicate two line AoEs hitting the sides of the boss.
*Disassembly is used again.

* A combination of the triangle AoE used before and a new attack in which three electric portals will spawn to the north, indicating line AoEs. Players must position to avoid both AoE sets at once. During this, each player will also receive a spread AoE marker (Static Spark).
*Amalgam becomes whole again.
*Amalgamight: Telegraphed physical tankbuster.
*Disassembly is used again, now also causing three sets of baited circle AoEs to appear beneath players. This is then followed with the same triangle/line AoEs and spread markers as before.
*Superbolt: Stack marker AoE dealing magical damage.
*Ternary Charge: A telegraphed point-blank AoE followed by two telegraphed concentric donut AoEs.

payload.name: Eliminator
payload.summary: *Disruption: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edges of the arena. *Partition: The boss's sword will begin glowing, indicating a late telegraphed half-room cleave at the right of the arena. *Reconfigured Partition: The boss's sword will switch direction and cleave the left of the arena.
encounter_notes: *Disruption: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edges of the arena.
*Partition: The boss's sword will begin glowing, indicating a late telegraphed half-room cleave at the right of the arena.
*Reconfigured Partition: The boss's sword will switch direction and cleave the left of the arena.

*Subroutine: The boss's floating hand (Elimination Claw) will move to west/east wall and begin charging energy, indicating a line AoE (Terminate) through where it is facing. In addition, the boss will cast another Reconfigured Partition, causing both AoEs to resolve at once, leaving two corners safe.

*Subroutine: Begins another set of AoEs. The boss's floating node (Elimbit) will converge lasers near the north/south wall, indicating a donut AoE (Halo of Destruction). Meanwhile, the boss will cast another Partition, leaving only half of the middle of the donut safe. After the AoEs resolve, each player is given a spread AoE marker (Electray) that deals magical damage and inflicts lightning resistance down Lightning Resistance Down II, making overlap lethal.
*Overexposure: Line stack marker on a random player, dealing magical damage.
*Subroutine: The boss becomes untargetable and summons six Lightning Generators that need to be killed before the Charge gauge reaches 100.
**During this sequence, players will need to dodge donut AoEs from the Elimbit and line AoEs from the Elimination Claw which have the same indicators as before.

**Later on, the Elimbit will reappear and use a telegraphed line AoE (Light of Salvation) hitting all players, so the party should spread. There will be another line stack marker as well although it is possible to skip this with enough DPS.
*The boss will become targetable again and use Holo Ark dealing high party-wide magical damage. This attack will wipe the party if the adds were not killed in time.

*Impact: A blue knockback circle will appear on one side. The knockback can be prevented with knockback immune actions. Meanwhile, each player will be targeted with Light of Salvation so should spread after the knockback.
*Elimination: Party-wide magical damage and spawns three sets of purple lines on the arena. These explode sequentially as line AoEs.

*Subroutine is used again but will now include all three previous AoEs: the boss's half-room cleave, the donut, and the hand line AoE. Players should resolve the first two and the move out of the hand line AoE, which will hit the initial safe spot from the donut.

payload.name: Prime Punutiy
payload.summary: *Punutiy Press: Party-wide magical damage. *Hydrowave: Faces a player and uses a telegraphed conal AoE. *Resurface: Moves to the deep water at the west of the arena and uses a telegraphed persistent conal AoE that inflicts heavy. The boss will suck in debris and foliage. Afterwards multiple circle and line AoE telegraphs will spawn, requiring players to dodge. Finally, an untargetable Ihuykatumu Flytrap add will spawn and use a telegraphed donut AoE (Decay).
encounter_notes: *Punutiy Press: Party-wide magical damage.
*Hydrowave: Faces a player and uses a telegraphed conal AoE.

*Resurface: Moves to the deep water at the west of the arena and uses a telegraphed persistent conal AoE that inflicts heavy. The boss will suck in debris and foliage. Afterwards multiple circle and line AoE telegraphs will spawn, requiring players to dodge. Finally, an untargetable Ihuykatumu Flytrap add will spawn and use a telegraphed donut AoE (Decay).
*The boss immediately follows with another Hydrowave.

*Song of the Punutiy: Summons four untargetable adds: two Prodigious Punutiy, one Petit Punutiy, and one Punutiy. Each add will tether and mark one player, along with spawning an AoE telegraph. Two players will be hit with large circle AoEs (Punutiy Flop), one with a medium circle AoE (Punutiy Flop), and one with a conal AoE (Hydrowave). Spread out to avoid overlap. Afterwards, the adds will become targetable and should be killed.
*Shore Shaker: A telegraphed point-blank AoE followed by two telegraphed concentric donut AoEs.

payload.name: Drowsie
payload.summary: The boss will initially be sleeping but will awake when pulled. *Uppercut: Telegraphed tankbuster. *Sow: Scatters four seeds on the ground.
encounter_notes: The boss will initially be sleeping but will awake when pulled.
*Uppercut: Telegraphed tankbuster.
*Sow: Scatters four seeds on the ground.

*Drowsy Dance: Four telegraphed AoE circles appear, denoting locations where the seeds will sprout into untargetable Ihuykatumu Ivy adds. Each add will have an orange target ring denoting where they are facing. They will use Wallop a late telegraphed line AoE in front of them.
* The adds will enlarge and may also turn to face a different direction. They will use Wallop again, but the AoEs will be larger, making the safe spots smaller.
*Sneeze: Telegraphed wide conal AoE from the boss.

*Spit: Spawns numerous untargetable Red Clots, Blue Clots, and Green Clots. They will use Metamorphosis and each turn into a targetable Mimiclot add, which should be killed. The adds will spawn circle AoE telegraphs and unavoidable circle AoE markers on single players (Flagrant Spread).

payload.name: Apollyon
payload.summary: *Razor Zephyr: Faces a player and uses a telegraphed wide line AoE. *Blade: Telegraphed tankbuster dealing high damage. *Wild beasts emerge to defend their territory... Three untargetable adds appear: two Ihuykatumu Pumas and one Ihuykatumu Ocelot, which begin attacking the boss.
encounter_notes: *Razor Zephyr: Faces a player and uses a telegraphed wide line AoE.
*Blade: Telegraphed tankbuster dealing high damage.
*Wild beasts emerge to defend their territory... Three untargetable adds appear: two Ihuykatumu Pumas and one Ihuykatumu Ocelot, which begin attacking the boss.
*High Wind: Party-wide physical damage. Also kills the adds.
*The boss will begin eating the adds, empowering itself as indicated by the system message:

*Swarming Locust: Jumps three times around the edge of the arena, then uses four telegraphed line AoEs hitting most of the arena (Blades of Famine), creating safe spots to its southwest and southeast. The boss will then repeat this sequence.
*Levinsickle: Spawns four circle AoEs. Two of them will leave behind lingering lightning AoEs, which each spawn two sets of four telegraphed conal AoEs. Dodge into the first set.
*Thunder III: Spread marker on each player.
*Sandworms burst from the ground, drawn by the vibrations above... Three untargetable Ihuykatumu Sandworm adds appear.
*The boss uses High Wind again, killing the adds.
*The boss will begin eating the adds, empowering itself as indicated by the system message:
*Blade: Telegraphed AoE tankbuster dealing high damage and inflicting windburn. Then spawns a telegraphed donut AoE (Wind Sickle) on the tank.
*Razor Storm: Jumps to the wall and uses a wide telegraphed frontal cleave.

*Windwhistle: An untargetable Whirlwind add will spawn and begin rotating. Standing in the add will deal damage (Biting Wind) and knock the player back. While moving, it will telegraph 8 line AoEs (Cutting Wind) in a diffuse starburst pattern. There are 3 sets of AoEs in total.
*While the Whirlwind is active, the boss will use Razor Zephyr, followed by the Thunder III spread AoEs. These occur in between the Cutting Wind AoEs from the add.

payload.name: Herpekaris
payload.summary: *Strident Shriek: Party-wide magical damage. *Vasoconstrictor: Spawns two poison globs in front of it, one left and one right. Standing in these will inflict File:Toxicosis icon1.png toxicosis damage-over-time for 15s. *Venomspill: The boss raises either its left or right leg, indicating which poison puddle will be hit, causing it to release multiple late telegraph circle AoEs (Pod Burst) in semi-random locations on its half of the room and partially covering the other half.
encounter_notes: *Strident Shriek: Party-wide magical damage.
*Vasoconstrictor: Spawns two poison globs in front of it, one left and one right. Standing in these will inflict File:Toxicosis icon1.png toxicosis damage-over-time for 15s.

*Venomspill: The boss raises either its left or right leg, indicating which poison puddle will be hit, causing it to release multiple late telegraph circle AoEs (Pod Burst) in semi-random locations on its half of the room and partially covering the other half.
**This attack will be used multiple times in succession.

**You should position yourself somewhere in the middle and immediately start moving to the safe side (edge of the arena of the safe side as AoEs can cover a bigger area). When the AoEs go off you should quickly start moving to the middle to be able to get to the other side for the next Venomspill. The last Venomspill will likely be on the same side as the previous one.
*Writhing Riot: Telegraphs three sequential AoEs: a 90-degree rear cone and two ~210-degree sweeps from its left or right.
*Poison Heart: Spread marker on all players. Used during Venomspill.
*Collective Agony: Line stack AoE marker dealing magical damage.
*Convulsive Crush: Telegraphed physical tankbuster.

payload.name: Deceiver
payload.summary: *Electrowave: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE on the edge of the arena, inflicting paralysis on anyone who steps in it. *Bionic Thrash: The boss will hover its tentacle arms over two opposite quadrants of the arena, indicating late telegraph AoEs. *Initialize Androids: Spawns a row of untargetable Origenics Sentry G9 adds at the north wall. Adjacent adds will be blurry, while all adds will telegraph a line AoE (Synchroshot), together covering the arena. Players should move in front of the blurry adds because their AoEs will not go off.
encounter_notes: *Electrowave: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE on the edge of the arena, inflicting paralysis on anyone who steps in it.
*Bionic Thrash: The boss will hover its tentacle arms over two opposite quadrants of the arena, indicating late telegraph AoEs.

*Initialize Androids: Spawns a row of untargetable Origenics Sentry G9 adds at the north wall. Adjacent adds will be blurry, while all adds will telegraph a line AoE (Synchroshot), together covering the arena. Players should move in front of the blurry adds because their AoEs will not go off.
*Afterwards, the adds will become targetable and should be killed.

*Initialize Turrets: Spawns four rectangular turrets on the west wall. Two turrets will be blurry, while all turrets will telegraph a line AoE, together covering the arena. Players should move in front of the blurry turrets because their AoEs will not go off.
**Immediately followed by the same attack with turret spawns in the opposite wall.

*Surge: Telegraphed horizontal knockback from the middle. Players should position to be knocked back into a non-blurry (real) turret to avoid hitting the border AoE. In addition, all players receive a spread AoE marker (Electray).

*Initialize Androids is used again, this time leaving only two blurry sentries. In addition, the boss will telegraph Bionic Thrash, leaving a smaller safe area from both the sentries and tentacle cleaves.

payload.name: Ambrose the Undeparted
payload.summary: *Psychic Wave: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE on the edge of the arena. *Overwhelming Charge: Late telegraph 180 degree frontal cleave. Get behind. *Psychokinesis: One cage in the west side, and one cage from the east, will begin jiggling, indicating two late telegraph line AoEs leaving one row safe. The cages will release one Origenics Eyeborg and two Superfluity adds, which should be killed.
encounter_notes: *Psychic Wave: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE on the edge of the arena.
*Overwhelming Charge: Late telegraph 180 degree frontal cleave. Get behind.

*Psychokinesis: One cage in the west side, and one cage from the east, will begin jiggling, indicating two late telegraph line AoEs leaving one row safe. The cages will release one Origenics Eyeborg and two Superfluity adds, which should be killed.

*Extrasensory Field: The arena will be divided into four blue quadrants, each with a different knockback arrow direction. The knockback is approximately half the long vertical of the arena. Players will need to position to avoid being knocked into the wall (by being pushed along the vertical) or use knockback immune.
*Voltaic Slash: Telegraphed physical tankbuster.
*Psychokinetic Charge: A combination of Extrasensory Fluid and Overwhelming Charge, where players must avoid being knocked back into the wall or the boss's subsequent frontal cleave.
*Electrolance: Massive telegraphed circle AoE at the back of the arena, causing a lance to appear.
*Psychokinesis: The boss spawns several red lines that briefly appear and disappear, telegraphing several line AoEs (Rush) from the lance.
*Psychokinesis with the cages is used again, but each player will also receive a spread AoE marker (Whorl of the Mind) dealing magical damage.
*Psychokinetic Charge is used again with another set of spread AoE markers.

payload.name: Barreltender
payload.summary: *Barbed Bellow: Party-wide magical damage. *Heavyweight Needles: Spawns multiple telegraphed conal AoEs, leaving gaps in between. Some gaps will be larger than others. Shortly before the cast resolves, the conal AoEs will expand and cover the smaller gaps, so players should stand in the middle of the largest gaps. This attack also spawns spines at the edges of the arena that will inflict bleed bleeding to anyone who steps in them. *Tender Drop: Drops multiple cacti on the arena. Most will have spines and a flower on top, while two will be naked.
encounter_notes: *Barbed Bellow: Party-wide magical damage.

*Heavyweight Needles: Spawns multiple telegraphed conal AoEs, leaving gaps in between. Some gaps will be larger than others. Shortly before the cast resolves, the conal AoEs will expand and cover the smaller gaps, so players should stand in the middle of the largest gaps. This attack also spawns spines at the edges of the arena that will inflict bleed bleeding to anyone who steps in them.
*Tender Drop: Drops multiple cacti on the arena. Most will have spines and a flower on top, while two will be naked.

*Barrel Breaker: Telegraphed radial knockback from the middle. Position to be knocked back towards a naked cactus, because each of the cacti will use a late telegraph point-blank AoE (Needle Storm), with the spiked and flowered cacti AoEs being larger (Needle Superstorm), leaving only some corners safe. Can also preposition near a naked cactus and use knockback resist.
*Succulent Stomp: Gives a random player a stack marker and jumps on them, dealing split physical damage.

*Prickly Left or Prickly Right: An initial half-room cleave telegraph in the direction of the cast that expands into a wide sweep hitting most of the arena except for a narrow conal region directly opposite the name of the cast.
*Tender Fury: Telegraphed physical tankbuster.

*Tender Drop is used again and combined with Heavyweight Needles, so players will need to position in the largest gaps that are close to a naked cacti. The cacti point-blank AoEs will go off a couple seconds after the conal AoEs.

payload.name: Anthracite
payload.summary: Players should note the circle and square holes on the arena and corresponding shaped holes in the walls, which will be used frequently for mechanics in this fight. *Anthrabomb: Spawns three black circle symbols and arrows, indicating where it will drop bombs that explode as large, late telegraphed circle AoEs. *Anthrabomb: Now spawns a yellow arrow leading towards a circle or square well, indicating it will throw a bomb in it, which will explode as late telegraphed line AoEs originating from the alternating wall holes of the same shape.
encounter_notes: Players should note the circle and square holes on the arena and corresponding shaped holes in the walls, which will be used frequently for mechanics in this fight.
*Anthrabomb: Spawns three black circle symbols and arrows, indicating where it will drop bombs that explode as large, late telegraphed circle AoEs.

*Anthrabomb: Now spawns a yellow arrow leading towards a circle or square well, indicating it will throw a bomb in it, which will explode as late telegraphed line AoEs originating from the alternating wall holes of the same shape.

*Anthrabomb: Now spawns two black arrows/circles and one yellow arrow, which is a combination of the first two usages of this ability. Players must dodge both the point-blank AoEs on the ground and the line AoEs from the wall holes at the same time.
*Carbonaceous Combustion: Party-wide magical damage.

*Carniflagration: Similar to the third usage of Anthrabomb (both black and yellow arrows) but used three times in a row. The next set of arrow telegraphs will appear shortly before the previous AoEs resolve, so players will need to consider the order of mechanics and dodge accordingly. Before the third set of AoEs resolve, each player will also be given a spread AoE marker (Anthrabomb).
*Burning Coals: Stack marker on a random player, dealing magical damage.
*Chimney Smack: Telegraphed magical tankbuster.

payload.name: Greatest Serpent of Tural
payload.summary: *Dubious Tulidisaster: Party-wide magical damage and spawns spikes at the edges of the arena that will inflict bleed bleeding to anyone who steps in them. *Bouncy Council: Spawns four untargetable clones, each of which will begin telegraphing a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line AoE (Misplaced Mystery) based on the blue arrows over its head. *Screes of Fury: Telegraphed AoE magical tankbuster.
encounter_notes: *Dubious Tulidisaster: Party-wide magical damage and spawns spikes at the edges of the arena that will inflict bleed bleeding to anyone who steps in them.
*Bouncy Council: Spawns four untargetable clones, each of which will begin telegraphing a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line AoE (Misplaced Mystery) based on the blue arrows over its head.
*Screes of Fury: Telegraphed AoE magical tankbuster.
*Bouncy Council: Now spawns four untargetable clones, each of which will begin telegraphing a point-blank AoE, as indicated by the spinning blue arrows. Move to the corner without a clone.

*Greatest Labyrinth: Pulls all players to the middle of the room. Spawns green arrows in different directions on the arena tiles (except for the middle 4 squares), purple X symbols on three corners, and a blue O symbol on one corner tile. Each player will receive link= Greatest Curse that lasts for 15s. They must cleanse this debuff before it naturally expires or they will instantly die. To cleanse the debuff, players must use the green arrows to transport them to the corner O tile. Touching the X tiles will inflict poison poison, dealing high damage-over-time. The symbols will disappear after the mechanic resolves.
**The easiest way to solve this is to locate the blue O tile corner work backwards, following the arrows that point to it until they reach the center of the room to find the safe path.
**Once you have reached the blue O tile, you may safely return to the center of the labyrinth and start attacking the boss once more, without waiting for the maze to disappear.
*Bouncy Council: Now spawns four clones in the 4 quadrants of the room. Two of these, always adjacent to each other, will use point-blank AoEs, while the other two use line AoEs.

*Moist Summoning: Spawns an untargetable Great Serpent of Tural add, which will use three sequential stack AoEs on a random player (Mighty Blorp) dealing physical damage and leaving behind a puddle. Each new puddle will be smaller than the last. Players who linger in this puddle for too long will receive sludge sludge for 15s, dealing damage-over-time. The add will disappear after this mechanic.

*Greatest Flood: Telegraphed radial knockback from one corner. Position to be knocked back while avoiding the lingering puddles, or use a knockback immunity ability. The puddles will disappear after this mechanic.

*Bouncy Council: Now spawns five clones, 4 in the quadrants of the room and one in the center. Two adjacent quadrant ones will use a point-blank AoE, while the other two quadrant ones and the center one will use line AoEs.
*Great Torrent: Spawns numerous sequential AoEs that cover the arena. Move into the first when it goes off. Also gives each player a spread AoE marker.

payload.name: Feather Ray
payload.summary: *Immersion: Party-wide magical damage. *Troublesome Tail: Gives each player a File:Nuisance icon.png Nuisance debuff with the combat message: . This debuff causes each player to mirror the boss's next attack. *Worrisome Wave: A telegraphed frontal conal AoE on a random player. Nuisance will cause each player will shoot a narrow untelegraphed conal AoE in front of them once their overhead timer expires. Players should avoid facing others.
encounter_notes: *Immersion: Party-wide magical damage.
*Troublesome Tail: Gives each player a File:Nuisance icon.png Nuisance debuff with the combat message: . This debuff causes each player to mirror the boss's next attack.

*Worrisome Wave: A telegraphed frontal conal AoE on a random player. Nuisance will cause each player will shoot a narrow untelegraphed conal AoE in front of them once their overhead timer expires. Players should avoid facing others.
*Hydro Ring: Telegraphed donut AoE that spawns a dangerous AoE at the edge of the arena, compressing it to a smaller circle.
*Blowing Bubbles: Numerous bubbles will originate from the boss and slowly move out, requiring players to dodge. The arena will return to normal when this attack ends.
*Bubble Bomb: Spawns multiple floating bubbles in a grid formation, leaving some empty spots.

*Rolling Current: A current from the east will shift all bubbles west by one position. Players will need to identify the empty spots considering the shift, because each bubble will explode in a late telegraphed point-blank AoE.
*Hydro Bomb then Troublesome Tail are used again, giving everyone File:Nuisance icon.png Nuisance.
*Trouble Bubbles: Each player will periodically shoot two slow-moving bubbles in front of where they are facing. Players must avoid being hit by others' bubbles.

payload.name: Firearms
payload.summary: *Dynamic Dominance: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edge of the arena. *Mirror Maneuver: Spawns a blue mirror on one wall and a yellow orb on one corner. The boss will jump to a corner adjacent to the yellow orb and aim a telegraphed line AoE (Thunderlight Burst) at the mirror. This will cause it to be reflected (with a late telegraph) and hit the orb, causing it to explode as a massive late telegraphed point-blank AoE. Players can avoid by standing directly opposite the orb. *Ancient Artillery: Spawns an orange arrowkey-like glyph on two tiles. These indicate plus-shaped AoEs originating from them.
encounter_notes: *Dynamic Dominance: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edge of the arena.

*Mirror Maneuver: Spawns a blue mirror on one wall and a yellow orb on one corner. The boss will jump to a corner adjacent to the yellow orb and aim a telegraphed line AoE (Thunderlight Burst) at the mirror. This will cause it to be reflected (with a late telegraph) and hit the orb, causing it to explode as a massive late telegraphed point-blank AoE. Players can avoid by standing directly opposite the orb.
*Ancient Artillery: Spawns an orange arrowkey-like glyph on two tiles. These indicate plus-shaped AoEs originating from them.
*Emergent Artillery: The glyphs will expand in the direction of the arrows and explode.
*Pummel: Telegraphed physical tankbuster.
*Mirror Maneuver: Now spawns two blue mirrors and three yellow orbs. Thunderlight Burst will now be reflected twice. Players will need to identify the orb that will be hit and move away from it.

*Ancient Artillery: Now spawns three glyphs instead of two, leaving only one tile safe. In addition, each player will be given a spread marker (Thunderblight Flurry) that will resolve after the tiles explode.

payload.name: Maulskull
payload.summary: Please note that players may fall off the arena to their death. As the boss has multiple knockback attacks, this may be problematic for less experienced parties. Knockbacks can be prevented using Arm's Length, Surecast, or Inner Release. *Stonecarver ( ): One of the boss' fists will begin glowing and make a sound effect, followed by the other one, indicating two sequential late telegraphed half-room cleaves. *Skullcrush: Spawns a blue knockback AoE circle at the north or the arena. Also gives each player a spread marker. Players will need to be knocked back leaning towards the southwest or southeast to avoid being knocked off. Note: The knockback is fairly long, so stand as close to the blue circle as possible. Afterwards the spread AoEs will resolve (Destructive Heat).
encounter_notes: Please note that players may fall off the arena to their death. As the boss has multiple knockback attacks, this may be problematic for less experienced parties. Knockbacks can be prevented using Arm's Length, Surecast, or Inner Release.
*Stonecarver ( ): One of the boss' fists will begin glowing and make a sound effect, followed by the other one, indicating two sequential late telegraphed half-room cleaves.

*Skullcrush: Spawns a blue knockback AoE circle at the north or the arena. Also gives each player a spread marker. Players will need to be knocked back leaning towards the southwest or southeast to avoid being knocked off. Note: The knockback is fairly long, so stand as close to the blue circle as possible. Afterwards the spread AoEs will resolve (Destructive Heat).

*Maulwork: The boss summons a large purple cube and punches it, telegraphing three sets of circle AoE. During the third set, either one two green arrow telegraphs will appear, indicating the location of wide line AoEs. This leaves either the sides or middle of the room safe.
*Deep Thunder: A tower with a multi-hit stack marker appears. The entire party should soak the tower, causing three hits of physical damage.
*Ringing Blows: A combination of Stonecarver half-room cleaves and Skullcrush knockback AoE (without the spread markers). Players will need to be knocked back safely then avoid the half-room cleaves.
*Wrought Fire: Telegraphed AoE magical tankbuster.

*Colossal Impact: A blue knockback circle will spawn near a lower corner of the arena. In addition, a stack marker will spawn on a random player. The party will need to be knocked back to the opposite corner while remaining stacked (Building Heat)
*Colossal Impact is used again, but this time, each player will receive a spread marker instead.
*Ashlayer: Party-wide magical damage.

payload.name: His Royal Headness Leonogg I
payload.summary: *Malicious Mist: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edge of the arena. *Falling Nightmare: Spawns a floating head above each player's location. After a few seconds, the head will drop from its spawn location (in a small late telegraphed circle AoE) and inflict File:Benoggined icon.png Benoggined for 10s, preventing anyone hit from taking actions and decreasing movement speed. Move away from the heads when they spawn to avoid. *Team Spirit: Summons several dolls around the arena.
encounter_notes: *Malicious Mist: Party-wide magical damage and spawns a dangerous AoE at the edge of the arena.

*Falling Nightmare: Spawns a floating head above each player's location. After a few seconds, the head will drop from its spawn location (in a small late telegraphed circle AoE) and inflict File:Benoggined icon.png Benoggined for 10s, preventing anyone hit from taking actions and decreasing movement speed. Move away from the heads when they spawn to avoid.
*Team Spirit: Summons several dolls around the arena.

*Spirited Charge: The dolls will begin running through the arena, aiming at certain players. Once each doll reaches the other side, it will run through the arena a second time. Anyone who touches them will be inflicted with bind for 5s, making them vulnerable to subsequent avoidable AoEs, and then inflicted with File:Benoggined icon.png Benoggined for 10s. This attack is combined with other mechanics throughout the fight, causing a very chaotic sequence of dodging multiple AoEs and dolls at once.
**The first time the dolls move, they will aim for the furthest player from them. The second time they move, they will aim for the closest player.

**Two ranged players can bait the dolls by standing near the north and south side of the arena, then move clockwise to dodge until the dolls reach the opposite wall. The dolls should aim for them again, so they can now dodge towards the middle of the arena.
Spirited Charge 1.jpg|Spirited Charge baits, step 1 (Credits to @The_Doddler)
Spirited Charge 2.jpg|Step 2

*Evil Scheme: Four exaflare AoE telegraphs will spawn in the middle, 90 degrees away from each other. This is followed by another set of exaflares in the previously empty areas. Wait for the first set of exaflares to go off twice then move into the spawn locations of the first set.
**Note that these AoEs resolve while the dolls are still running around, so it is important to not touch them.

*Team Spirit and Spirited Charge are used again. In addition, two players will receive Looming Nightmare, a five-hit series of chasing circle AoEs. Players must avoid both the AoEs and the dolls at once.

*Team Spirit and Spirited Charge are used again. In addition, the boss will telegraph three sets of sequential conal AoEs that cover the arena (Scream). Players must avoid both the AoEs and the dolls at once. While the dolls are still running around, two players will receive Looming Nightmare.
*Falling Nightmare is used again but now summons heads at various locations above the arena, which should be dodged accordingly.

payload.name: Jack-in-the-Pot
payload.summary: *Troubling Teacups: Spawns four teacups at the edges of the arena on the cardinals. *Tea Awhirl: A ghost appears, tethers, and possesses one teacup. Afterward, all of the tea cups will begin spinning multiple times, moving inwards and outwards to attempt to disorient players. Players must keep track of the originally tethered teacup during this sequence because it will explode as a large late telegraphed AoE (Tricksome Treat). *Troubling Teacups: Now spawns eight teacups, two per cardinal.
encounter_notes: *Troubling Teacups: Spawns four teacups at the edges of the arena on the cardinals.

*Tea Awhirl: A ghost appears, tethers, and possesses one teacup. Afterward, all of the tea cups will begin spinning multiple times, moving inwards and outwards to attempt to disorient players. Players must keep track of the originally tethered teacup during this sequence because it will explode as a large late telegraphed AoE (Tricksome Treat).
*Troubling Teacups: Now spawns eight teacups, two per cardinal.

**Tea Awhirl: Two teacups will now be possessed by ghosts. Similar to before, players must keep track of where the possessed teacups end up because both of them will explode. The two tethered teacups will either be 90 or 180 degrees apart, so the final set of AoEs will also spawn in the safe offset.

** An easy solution to this mechanic is to observe just the first teacup (if possessed cups are next to each other) or any of them if they are on opposite sides. When the cups start to stop go 90 degrees ahead of the observed cup (where another, safe cup will be present) on the edge of the encounter area.
*Toiling Teapots: Spawns 13 teacups, nine on the cardinals/center and four on the intercardinals.

**Kettles will appear over some cups and begin pouring a purple liquid into them, causing them to overflow and create an expanding puddle AoE. While these expand, more cups will be filled and overflow to create more puddles, followed by the remaining cups. Anyone who contacts a puddle will receive damage (Mad Tea Party) and be inflicted with bleeding damage-over-time for 15s.
**Players should stand near the cups to be filled last and move into the previous puddle locations when they disappear.
**The boss will use Last Drop, a telegraphed magical tankbuster, during this.
*Troubling Teacups / Tea Awhirl is repeated again and functions similarly to its second incarnation. However, the ghosts will now tether two teacups on opposite cardinals.
*Sordid Steam: Party-wide magical damage.
Strayborough Deadwalk boss 2 patterns.png|All possible Troubling Teacups patterns and safe areas (Credits to Reddit user /u/Sovis)

payload.name: Träumerei
payload.summary: *Bitter Regret: A large blue portal will spawn at the north, indicating a line AoE leaving the sides safe. This attack repeats, summoning two portals at the sides (with the boss also hovering its arms over the arena), leaving the middle safe. *Poltergeist: The boss possesses debris and drops them on the arena (as telegraphed line AoEs), partitioning it into four quadrants. * The ghost panels on each quadrant will light up, and each player will be tethered to an untargetable Stray Geist add on their quadrant. Players must sufficiently stretch their tethers so it turns purple to avoid taking high damage (Ill Intent). However, this requires them to first step into a ghost panel, inflicting File:Ghostly guise icon.png Ghostly Guise, allowing them to pass through the debris blocking other quadrants and enabling them to stretch their tethers.
encounter_notes: *Bitter Regret: A large blue portal will spawn at the north, indicating a line AoE leaving the sides safe. This attack repeats, summoning two portals at the sides (with the boss also hovering its arms over the arena), leaving the middle safe.
*Poltergeist: The boss possesses debris and drops them on the arena (as telegraphed line AoEs), partitioning it into four quadrants.

* The ghost panels on each quadrant will light up, and each player will be tethered to an untargetable Stray Geist add on their quadrant. Players must sufficiently stretch their tethers so it turns purple to avoid taking high damage (Ill Intent). However, this requires them to first step into a ghost panel, inflicting File:Ghostly guise icon.png Ghostly Guise, allowing them to pass through the debris blocking other quadrants and enabling them to stretch their tethers.

*Ghostduster: Each player will be given a large spread AoE marker. If they are hit by this with File:Ghostly guise icon.png Ghostly Guise, they will instantly die. Players must return to physical form by stepping on a ghost panel again to survive.
*Malicious Mist: Party-wide magical damage that also inflicts bleeding.

*Memorial March: Spawns multiple Stray Phantagenitrix at the north wall in two alternating groups. The first group will being floating up and charging a line AoE attack (Bitter Regret) followed by the other set. This will be combined with a Bitter Regret from the boss itself, leaving the middle or sides safe after the last set of smaller line AoEs.
*Fleshbuster: An attack that will instantly kill anyone without File:Ghostly guise icon.png Ghostly Guise. Players must step on the ghost panels to re-acquire the buff if needed.

*Poltergeist is used again, partitioning the arena in to quadrants. However, this time, Stray Phantagenitrix will appear on half of the arena. Players must resolve the proximity tethers from the Stray Geist adds while avoiding the half of the room covered by the line AoEs.
*Ghostcrusher: Line stack AoE marker on one player, dealing magical damage.
*The proximity tethers will spawn again, and can be resolved as before. However, this will now also be combined with a Bitter Regret AoE from the boss, which goes off after the tethers.

payload.name: Gargant
payload.summary: *Chilling Chirp: Party-wide magical damage. *Almighty Racket: The boss will face a random player and use a late telegraphed 180 degree frontal cleave. Get behind. *The boss will then become untargetable, jump outside the arena, and begin crawling around. Take note of its location, as the sand falls will obscure it. When it stops (always behind a sand fall), it will re-emerge and use a late telegraphed wide line AoE charge (Aerial Assault) through the arena.
encounter_notes: *Chilling Chirp: Party-wide magical damage.

payload.name: Ambujam
payload.summary: * Big Wave: Moderate damage to the entire party and inflicts a weak bleeding Bleeding damage over time effect. * Tentacle Dig: Ambujam submerges one or both of its larger tentacles and moves them around, denoted by ripples in the water. Eventually the tentacles will stop moving and after a few seconds erupt into large circle AoEs that deal high damage and inflict a strong File:Toxicosis icon1.png Toxicosis damage over time debuff. * Toxic Fountain: Three sets of circle AoEs appear and burst with high damage and knockback in the order they appeared.
encounter_notes: * Big Wave: Moderate damage to the entire party and inflicts a weak bleeding Bleeding damage over time effect.

* Tentacle Dig: Ambujam submerges one or both of its larger tentacles and moves them around, denoted by ripples in the water. Eventually the tentacles will stop moving and after a few seconds erupt into large circle AoEs that deal high damage and inflict a strong File:Toxicosis icon1.png Toxicosis damage over time debuff.
* Toxic Fountain: Three sets of circle AoEs appear and burst with high damage and knockback in the order they appeared.

To predict the Tentacle Dig safe spots, look at the patterns in the water. Each tentacle can start at either the boss's left flank-midpoint ("flank midpoint" being the arrows at the exact left/right of his hitbox circle) or the boss's right flank-midpoint. After that, the tentacles will head towards the opposite flank-midpoint, but they can do so along one of two possible paths:

* From the starting flank-midpoint (left/right "arrows" of boss's hitbox) they can go along the OUTSIDE of the boss's hitbox first, then reach the opposite flank-midpoint, then go INTO the boss's hitbox as they turn towards the side of the boss where they passed by earlier. Example: the water ripples start at boss's left flank-midpoint, then proceed clockwise along the boss's hitbox (along the boss's front side); then it reaches the boss's right flank-midpoint, goes into the boss's hitbox, and takes a sharp turn towards the front of the boss. If you notice this path (if you see that the waves in the water proceed along the OUTSIDE of the boss's hitbox), the safe spot will be on the side opposite where the tentacle started (in the previous example, move to the boss's right side)

* From the starting flank-midpoint they can take a sharper turn INTO the boss's hitbox, then go (from within the boss's hitbox) to the opposite flank-midpoint, and then make another turn towards the side of the boss where they entered the circle of the boss's hitbox. Example: the water ripples start at boss's right flank-midpoint, then proceed for a short while clockwise; when they reach the point of the boss's hitbox where the right flank becomes rear they turn into the boss's hitbox, and proceed towards the boss's left flank-midpoint; then they go outside the boss's hitbox and head towards the boss's rear. If you notice this path (if you see that the waves in the water went into the boss's hitbox to reach the opposite flank-midpoint), the safe spot will be on the same side as where the tentacles started (in the previous example, move to the boss's right side)

Since there has to always be a safe spot, the quickest way to identify the safe spot (even when there is two tentacles) is to simply identify which of the ripples in the water is going along the outside of the boss's hitbox -- if it starts from the left flank-midpoint (information 1), and goes clockwise along the front side of the boss's hitbox (information 2), putting together these two bits of information you can predict that the safe spot will be to the right/slightly bottom-right of the boss's side. When there are two tentacles, the second tentacle will hit an area in such a way that only one of the far sides of the arena (far right or far left) will be safe from both AoEs -- the safe side is the one opposite where the aforementioned tentacle (the one that goes half a circle around and OUTSIDE the boss's hitbox) started. So, in conclusion: whichever side (left or right) of the boss's flank-midpoint the tentacle going along the OUTSIDE of the boss's hitbox originated from, the far opposite side of the arena will always be the safe spot.

payload.name: Armored Chariot

At the same time, several clockwork Death Claws will appear in the corners, facing the boss. These Death Claws will be marked with pips, either 1 or 2. The Armored Chariot will create violet shields and turn them to face the Death Claws, which in turn fire a large laser. The laser reflects off the shield, creating a cone AoE in that quadrant of the arena. The lasers deal damage over time while standing in them, and will also inflict a strong Sustained Damage damage over time debuff. After the first set of Death Claws fire, the Chariot will rotate its shields to the second set and repeat the process. ** The second cast of this ability only summons two Death Claws in opposing corners, but also adds several other Death Claws that aim across the arena and not at the Chariot. All of the Death Claws will fire at the same time, leaving narrow safe spots next to the Death Claws not firing directly at the boss. Subsequent casts alternate between the first and second versions. * Diffusion Ray: Mode
encounter_notes: * Articulated Bits: The Armored Chariot moves to the center of the arena and creates an electricity puddle inside its hitbox, which inflicts an electrocution Electrocution damage over time debuff. At the same time, several clockwork Death Claws will appear in the corners, facing the boss. These Death Claws will be marked with pips, either 1 or 2. The Armored Chariot will create violet shields and turn them to face the Death Claws, which in turn fire a large laser. The lasers deal damage over time while standing in them, and will also inflict a strong Sustained Damage damage over time debuff. After the first set of Death Claws fire, the Chariot will rotate its shields to the second set and repeat the process.

** The second cast of this ability only summons two Death Claws in opposing corners, but also adds several other Death Claws that aim across the arena and not at the Chariot. All of the Death Claws will fire at the same time, leaving narrow safe spots next to the Death Claws not firing directly at the boss. Subsequent casts alternate between the first and second versions.
* Diffusion Ray: Moderate damage to the entire party.
* Graviton Cannon: Targeted circle AoEs on each player. Used alongside every other Articulated Bits cast from the third onward.
* Rail Cannon: Tankbuster

payload.name: Kapikulu
payload.summary: The boss's arena is full of spike traps that inflict a bleeding Bleeding damage over time debuff if they are walked over. The spike traps along the edge of the arena are always active, while those in the center extend and retract as the boss uses its abilities. * Billowing Bolts: Moderate damage to the entire party. * Spin Out: Kapikulu moves to the northern edge of the arena and pulls all players to him, wrapping everyone in ribbons and inflicting File:Fetters icon2.png Fetters. Several of the spike traps in the arena will extend spikes for this attack. Kapikulu will quickly unravel the ribbons, causing all players to begin uncontrollably File:Spinning icon1.png Spinning for 10 seconds. While spinning, the players slowly move automatically in the direction indicated by a pointing hand over their heads. Attempting to turn rotates the hand, which results in very loose turns. When the Spinning effect ends, all players become File:Dizzy icon1.png Dizzy for 2 seconds, preventing movement and the use of skills. Kapikulu will then return to the center of the arena and the spikes will retract.
encounter_notes: The boss's arena is full of spike traps that inflict a bleeding Bleeding damage over time debuff if they are walked over. The spike traps along the edge of the arena are always active, while those in the center extend and retract as the boss uses its abilities.
* Billowing Bolts: Moderate damage to the entire party.

* Spin Out: Kapikulu moves to the northern edge of the arena and pulls all players to him, wrapping everyone in ribbons and inflicting File:Fetters icon2.png Fetters. Several of the spike traps in the arena will extend spikes for this attack. Kapikulu will quickly unravel the ribbons, causing all players to begin uncontrollably File:Spinning icon1.png Spinning for 10 seconds. While spinning, the players slowly move automatically in the direction indicated by a pointing hand over their heads. Attempting to turn rotates the hand, which results in very loose turns. When the Spinning effect ends, all players become File:Dizzy icon1.png Dizzy for 2 seconds, preventing movement and the use of skills. Kapikulu will then return to the center of the arena and the spikes will retract.

** Basting Blade: The second cast of Spin Out will also have the boss use this attack. Kapikulu leaps to the opposite edge of the arena and fires a wide line attack directly across. Kapikulu will do this twice before the players' Spinning and Dizzy debuffs end.
* Crewel Slice: Tankbuster.

* Wild Weave: Several yellow and green ropes will descend from the ceiling. Kapikulu will tether to one of the ropes, causing an orb to fall from all other ropes of that color, which explode in large circle AoEs.
* Magnitude Opus: Stack marker on a random player.
* Rotary Gale: Targeted circle AoEs on each player.

The boss's line aoes in the second spinning attack are not truly "random" as they may appear the first times you play. The boss always hits the middle of the arena (and a small portion of the sides) first; then he will hit either side as second attack. Therefore, the ideal path to follow when spinning is to always spin all the way to the back of the arena, along the far left/far right sides of the arena, while the boss is doing the first line AoE. Then, as you are approaching the end of the arena (and while the boss is finishing the first attack/preparing his second one), make a U-turn (180°) with the goal to spin back to the front of the arena, along the middle column of the arena itself.

payload.name: Lyssa
payload.summary: * Skull Dasher: Tank Buster * Frigid Stomp: Room-wide AoE * Frostbite and Seek: The boss returns to the center of the arena and shrouds it in a snowstorm, then disappears. Shortly after, the boss will emerge from one of the six craters around the arena and cover it in a massive AoE that can only be avoided by standing behind the boss. Players can determine which crater the boss will emerge from by looking for the crater with no tracks leading away from it. If hit by this, players will take heavy damage and a Vulnerability Up debuff.
encounter_notes: * Skull Dasher: Tank Buster
* Frigid Stomp: Room-wide AoE

* Frostbite and Seek: The boss returns to the center of the arena and shrouds it in a snowstorm, then disappears. Shortly after, the boss will emerge from one of the six craters around the arena and cover it in a massive AoE that can only be avoided by standing behind the boss. Players can determine which crater the boss will emerge from by looking for the crater with no tracks leading away from it. If hit by this, players will take heavy damage and a Vulnerability Up debuff.
* Icicall: Three icicles spawn around the arena and fire point-blank AoEs. Following this they will either fire a straight line AoE across the edges of the arena or directly through the center.

* Heavy Smash: A random player receives a stack marker, requiring players to stack together to mitigate damage. This can occur during Icicall, and will resolve after the icicles have fired, so it is recommended to stack after the arena is clear.

payload.name: Ladon Lord
payload.summary: * Scratch: Tank Buster. * Intimidation: Room-wide AoE. * Pyric Blast: Stack marker
encounter_notes: * Scratch: Tank Buster.
* Intimidation: Room-wide AoE.
* Pyric Blast: Stack marker
* Inhale: The boss will inhale Aether, after which one or two of its heads will grow large and flames will issue from its mouths. This indicates which heads will perform Pyric Breath.

* Pyric Breath: The boss will leap to the center of the room, and once it begins casting, will face a direction and not turn. The heads that are swollen will cast a 120-degree fire AoE that fills an entire third of the room, with the normal heads indicating a safe zone to stand in. If the "side" heads are active (left and right head will fire), the spot in front of the boss is actually a safe area.
* Pyric Spheres: Summons four Pyric Spheres around the arena. They will fire cross-line AoEs across the arena, so players must stand in the spaces between to avoid.

payload.name: Hermes
payload.summary: After the boss's first Trismegistos, the edge of the arena will be covered in an AoE that inflicts a 15 second Windburn debuff that deals Damage over Time. * Trismegistos: Room-wide AoE. * Double: Augments the next spell cast.
encounter_notes: After the boss's first Trismegistos, the edge of the arena will be covered in an AoE that inflicts a 15 second Windburn debuff that deals Damage over Time.
* Trismegistos: Room-wide AoE.
* Double: Augments the next spell cast.
* Quadruple: Augments the next two spells cast.
* True Tornado: Tank Buster. If cast with Double, drops a circular AoE under the tank's feet after the cast, which should be dodged.
* True Bravery: Interruptible - The boss receives a damage up Damage Up buff that lasts for 20 seconds.

* True Aero: Each player will be marked by an unavoidable AoE line that must be spread out to avoid hitting other players. If the boss casts Double before this, after the lines fire, they will drop an additional line AoE that players can simply step out of to avoid.

* True Aero II: Players will be marked with point-blank AoEs and must spread out to avoid overlapping damage. If the boss cast Quadruple before this, after the initial AoEs resolve, another AoE will spawn that players must step out of.
* Meteor: 4 proximity markers around the edges of the arena. Run to the center to minimize damage from the meteors that will land. These meteors will block the damage from Hermetica.

* Hermetica: Summon large green panels at the edges of the arena. After a moment, these will fire a large line AoE across the platform, knocking back anyone hit. The boss will summon these in one of four patterns:

** Three sets of panels (a couple and two single ones) spawn at the edges of the arena and are offset so as not to fire through the centre of the arena. Simply stand in the center of the room to avoid.
** Two panels per side on two sides that fire through the center of the arena.

** (Double): Two sets of four panels. Players need to observe the order in which the sets are summoned, and break the Line of Sight of the panels in the order they were summoned. Players need to stand behind the meteor without the yellow cracks, as those meteors will shatter after the first attack, and players will not have enough time to move between the sets firing.

** (Quadruple): Four sets of two panels on each edge of the arena. These will fire in the order they are summoned, and players will need to stand in the center and dodge towards the opening next to each set of panels to avoid each blast.
These mechanics will repeat until the boss is defeated.

For the Quadruple panels attack, imagine the arena divided in four parts by an imaginary cross. Each couple of panels will fire a shot that will hit: the left half, the right half, the upper half, the lower half (not in this order). The position of the first shot is random, but the next ones are mostly predictable. If the first shot covers the left half, the second shot will never cover the right half (therefore it can either hit the lower half, or the upper half). If the second shot covers the upper half, the third shot will always cover the right half (the half that was safe from the first shot) and the fourth shot will always cover the lower half (the half that was safe from the second shot). One possible way to avoid moving too much and dodge everything is therefore like this:

1) Identify which quadrant is safe from the first two shots (only one of the four sections of the imaginary "cross" will be safe from the first two shots). If, for example, the first panels hit the left half and the second panels hit the lower half, the safe quadrant will be the upper right quadrant. The closer you can stay to the center (where the boss is), the better.
2) Let the first two shots fly.

3) Move to the opposite quadrant (in the previous example, move to the lower left quadrant) for the next two shots. There is a rather generous delay between each shot, so you will have plenty of time to move the necessary distance (provided you are close to the center, where the boss is) between the second and third shot.

payload.name: Albion
payload.summary: *Call of the Mountain: The screen will begin shaking and the system message "A rumbling in the distance draws closer..." will appear. A portion of the east or west wall will begin to have moving snow, telegraphing where a herd of animals will charge through the room as a line AoE that hits around a third of the arena. The system message "Another rumbling can be heard in the distance..." will then appear, and an animal herd will charge down another third of the room based on the telegraph. Anyone hit by the charging animals will be inflicted with File:Concussion icon1.png Concussion and receive damage-over-time. *Albion's Embrace: Telegraphed tankbuster *Left Slam / Right Slam: The boss will use a half-room cleave to the left or right of its hitbox, based on the name of the attack. Has only a brief AoE indicator.
encounter_notes: *Call of the Mountain: The screen will begin shaking and the system message "A rumbling in the distance draws closer..." will appear. A portion of the east or west wall will begin to have moving snow, telegraphing where a herd of animals will charge through the room as a line AoE that hits around a third of the arena. The system message "Another rumbling can be heard in the distance..." will then appear, and an animal herd will charge down another third of the room based on the telegraph. Anyone hit by the charging animals will be inflicted with File:Concussion icon1.png Concussion and receive damage-over-time.
*Albion's Embrace: Telegraphed tankbuster
*Left Slam / Right Slam: The boss will use a half-room cleave to the left or right of its hitbox, based on the name of the attack. Has only a brief AoE indicator.
*Knock on Ice: The boss summons three chunks of ice, telegraphed by red AoEs.
*Icebreaker: The boss faces one ice chunk, tethers it, and targets with a orange reticle. It will use a large circular AoE (with only a brief indicator) that destroys the rock.
*Icy Throes (no cast bar): The boss marks everyone with an AoE telegraph so the party should spread. Two more ice chunks will also spawn.
*Roar of Albion: A roomwide AoE that can be dodged by hiding behind an ice chunk from the boss.

payload.name: Galatea Magna
payload.summary: *Waxing Cycle: The boss will use a large, telegraphed point-blank AoE, immediately followed by a very briefly telegraphed donut AoE that hits the previously safe area. Anyone hit by this attack or the next one will be inflicted with Sustained Damage. *Waning Cycle: The boss will use a large, telegraphed donut AoE, immediately followed by a very briefly telegraphed donut AoE that hits the previously safe area. *Soul Scythe: The boss will face a random cardinal, then jump to it and perform a large, briefly telegraphed, circular AoE in the direction it was facing.
encounter_notes: *Waxing Cycle: The boss will use a large, telegraphed point-blank AoE, immediately followed by a very briefly telegraphed donut AoE that hits the previously safe area. Anyone hit by this attack or the next one will be inflicted with Sustained Damage.
*Waning Cycle: The boss will use a large, telegraphed donut AoE, immediately followed by a very briefly telegraphed donut AoE that hits the previously safe area.
*Soul Scythe: The boss will face a random cardinal, then jump to it and perform a large, briefly telegraphed, circular AoE in the direction it was facing.

*Soul Nebula: Unavoidable roomwide damage that also spawns will summon two portals to the boss's east and west. This is followed by Scarecrow Chase. Each portal will have a number of dots over it (1 or 2), indicating in which order the boss will teleport to them and use a briefly telegraphed cross AoE that hits the intercardinals of the portals. Anyone hit will be inflicted with Doom that must be cleansed with Esuna to prevent death. This first set can be dodged by remaining in the center of the room.

*Tenebrism: Gives everyone the File:Glassy-eyed icon1.png Glassy-eyed debuff. Four meteor circles will sequentially spawn around the boss and must be soaked by at least one player to prevent them from exploding and dealing party-wide damage. When the last tower is about to be soaked, gaze indicators will appear above everyone, indicating that their Glassy-eyed debuff will resolve soon. Everyone must look away from each other or they will be inflicted with Petrification.

*Soul Nebula / Scarecrow Chase (version 2): Functions similarly as before, except the boss will start on the edge of the arena and summon four portals, one in the middle, and three in the other edges.
Notes:

*Depending on how quickly the party kills the boss, it will give a different line of dialogue upon its defeat and rank the party's performance from 1 to 12, with a lower number being a faster kill time. This appears to be purely cosmetic and does not impact rewards.
*An average party in the Duty Finder will typically receive a rank of 7.

*The top rank of 1 requires a kill time of less than 90 seconds (at level 90, a premade party of 3+ DPS in item level 630-635 best-in-slot gear, food, tinctures, full resource openers, party buff alignment, and strong burst damage is typically needed to achieve this).
*If Zero is in the party as a Duty Support NPC, it will also give a different line of dialogue upon its defeat.

payload.name: Cagnazzo
payload.summary: Shortly after engaging the boss, the arena will be surrounded by an AoE that will inflict Dropsy and deal damage-over-time to anyone who steps in it. *Stygian Deluge: Unavoidable party-wide damage. *Antediluvian: Spawns three sets of two bubbles across the arena, which will grow in size. When a bubble reaches maximum size, it will drop down as a large circular AoE with a brief indicator. The boss will also spawn a purple knockback AoE in the middle (Body Slam), which will kill anyone inside the AoE telegraph. This knockback cannot be prevented with knockback immune actions.
encounter_notes: Shortly after engaging the boss, the arena will be surrounded by an AoE that will inflict Dropsy and deal damage-over-time to anyone who steps in it.
*Stygian Deluge: Unavoidable party-wide damage.

*Antediluvian: Spawns three sets of two bubbles across the arena, which will grow in size. When a bubble reaches maximum size, it will drop down as a large circular AoE with a brief indicator. The boss will also spawn a purple knockback AoE in the middle (Body Slam), which will kill anyone inside the AoE telegraph. This knockback cannot be prevented with knockback immune actions.
*Hydraulic Ram: The boss will sequentially telegraph several line charge and circle AoEs which will disappear after a short time. It will then use AoE attacks in the order of the telegraphs.
*Hydrofall: Telegraphed stack AoE.
*Cursed Tide: The boss assigns various debuffs to players and becomes untargetable.
**File:Neap tide icon1.png Neap Tide: A point-blank AoE on the afflicted player when the debuff expires. Three players will receive this.
**File:Spring tide icon1.png Spring Tide: A stack AoE on the afflicted player when the debuff expires. One player will receive this.
**The boss will spawn four immobile Fearsome Flotsam which must be defeated before Cagnazzo's Power reaches 100, or the party will wipe.
**The party's debuffs will resolve, but they will be telegraphed with standard AoE indicators for several seconds before they resolve.
**Several telegraphed circular AoEs will also spawn.
*Tsunami: Party-wide damage after the adds phase. Heal through and mitigate.
*Voidcleaver: Four portals will spawn, each tethering to one player. These will periodically spawn telegraphed conal AoEs in the direction of the tethered player.
*Lifescleaver: Multiple telegraphed conal AoEs originating from the boss.
*Void Torrent: Line AoE tankbuster.

payload.name: Face
payload.summary: * Lines of Fire: The boss will tether to the face statues outside of the arena, and several line AoEs will appear that force players into alignment with one of the statues. Getting hit by any of these will result in the death of the player. Once the beams fire, the face the player is in line with will debuff them with a stack of either File:Smiley face icon1.png Smiley Face (blue) or File:Frowny face icon1.png Frowny Face (red). Players must alternate between the two debuffs for the entire fight, as getting two stacks deals heavy damage, knocks the player back and debuffs with Down for the Count. Three stacks will K.O the player. * Off My Lawn: Knockback usually combined with targeted AoE for each player, spread out to avoid overlapping. Every use after the first will be combined with Lines of Fire to make your positioning even more difficult to figure out; anti-knockback works fine if the proper safe lane is out of melee range or otherwise inconvenient. * Temper's Flare: Raid-wide AoE.

* Temper's Flare: Raid-wide AoE.
* Upside Down: Turns the faces on the outside upside down so their color switches.
* Heart On Fire IV: Tankbuster.

payload.name: Frameworker
payload.summary: * Circular Saw: Raid-wide AoE. * Leap Forward: Jumps in the direction boss is facing and drop a massive AoE. Move to the opposite wall that the boss is facing to avoid. * Print Workers: Commands the two adds to copy the Leap mechanic.

* Left Disassembler: Cleave on the left side of the boss.
* Electric Arc: Stack.
* Levelling Missile Targeted AoEs on each player.
* Violent Discharge Raid-wide AoE.

payload.name: Lyngbakr

Will cause any crystals formed to cast a wide or small AoE dependent on crystal size. *Tidal Breath: Lyngbakr turns around and casts a Large arena-wide AoE with high damage to anyone not behind them.
